resale_co.name: Municipal Certificate of Continued Compliance (MCCC)
resale_co.issued_by: Municipal Certificate of Continued Compliance (MCCC) Office, Department of Community Development (Property Maintenance), 505 Sidney Road
resale_co.lead_time: Township strongly recommends applying at least 4 weeks before the closing date; an inspection date may be up to 10 days after the application is submitted
requirements: All utilities (gas, water, electric) must be on at the time of inspection
Gutters, downspouts, sidewalk, driveway, apron, stairs, chimney and siding in good condition
Screens on windows and doors of habitable rooms; all windows operable, no broken or cracked glass
Guardrails and graspable handrails on stairs with 4 or more risers or more than 30 inches high
House number at least 3 inches high on the house or mailbox
Tree limbs off the house; trees and shrubs cut back 12 inches from the house
Driveway must be paved or another hard surface (no stone or gravel)
GFCI outlets outdoors, in bathrooms, kitchens, laundry areas, garages, unfinished basements and within 6 feet of any sink
At least 2 outlets per habitable room; working lights in halls, stairs, baths, laundry and furnace rooms
No plumbing leaks; flexible drain piping must be replaced; water heater relief valve with extension within 6 inches of the floor
Gas shut-off valve behind gas stove and dryer; stove anti-tip bracket
Bath ventilation (window or fan); safety glazing on windows in tub or shower areas
Solid core or steel 20-minute rated door between garage and house
Smoke and CO alarms within 10 feet of sleeping areas and on every level including the basement; 10-year sealed battery alarms; hardwired alarms under 10 years old

Licensed-professional letters for the heating unit and fireplace, plus septic and well water test results if applicable; any work done without a required permit must be permitted and all permits closed

fees.label: MCCC, single-family home, condo or townhome
fees.quote: MCCC for a single-family home, condo, or townhome: $150 per unit

fees.label: MCCC, two-family
fees.quote: MCCC for a two-family: $150 per unit ($300 total)

fees.label: Temporary MCCC (after applying for an MCCC)
Reinspection, third inspection and each one after
fees.quote: Reinspections: $100 per unit from the third inspection and any following

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the 'Sale of Residential Property' MCCC application and bring or send it with the fee to the MCCC Office at the Public Works Center, 505 Sidney Road, Piscataway, NJ 08854. The office then schedules the inspection (Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. and 1:30 to 3:30 p.m.). The inspection report and approved MCCC are emailed to the owner.

evidence.quote: As of January 1, 2019, a Municipal Certificate of Continued Compliance (MCCC) is required when selling or renting a home in Piscataway to ensure the health, safety and general welfare of residents.

For an inspection appointment, please provide the completed MCCC application along with the appropriate fee to the Municipal Certificate of Continued Compliance (MCCC) Office in the Public Works Center.
Please note, if any work was performed without a permit and one was required, you will be required to obtain the permit and close any open permits before an MCCC will be issued.
Ben Pobicki Supervisor of Property Maintenance / MCCC 505 Sidney Rd (732) 562-2393
We strongly recommend the application be submitted a minimum of four (4) weeks prior to the closing date or four (4) weeks prior to the occupancy date for rentals.
SALE OF RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY MUNICIPAL CERTIFICATE OF CONTINUED COMPLIANCE (MCCC) Fee: $150 Single Family / Townhouse / Condo $300 Two Family

evidence.quote: Note: An inspection date may be up to 10 days from date application is submitted, depending on schedule availability.
All battery operated smoke alarms installed must be the sealed 10 year battery type. All hardwired (110v) smoke alarms must be less than 10 years old.

resale_co.notes: Piscataway renamed the program from 'Municipal Certificate of Continued Occupancy (MCCO)' to 'Municipal Certificate of Continued Compliance (MCCC)'; the old MCCO page address now returns 404. The same MCCC is also required for rentals (separate rental form and landlord registration), which is not a resale item. The checklist says it is partial and is only a guide. The sale form asks about open permits, well water and the approximate closing date. No validity period is published.

requirements: Township MCCC checklist: battery smoke alarms must be the sealed 10-year battery type; hardwired (110v) smoke alarms must be less than 10 years old and must not be replaced with battery alarms
Township MCCC checklist: smoke and CO alarms within 10 feet of each sleeping area and on each level of possible living space, including the basement even if unfinished (not attic or crawl space)

fire_cert.notes: The state LEA registry (July 2026) lists Piscataway as a municipal enforcing agency, and the state fire directory names the Fire Official, Matthew Jandernal, at 555 Sidney Rd. The Township's Fire Prevention Bureau pages only describe commercial and food-truck inspections and post no resale smoke/CO certificate form or fee. The MCCC resale checklist includes smoke and CO alarm rules citing N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3, so the smoke/CO check may be done as part of the MCCC inspection, but no official page says which office issues the state smoke/CO certificate or what it costs. The state directory lists the Fire Official email as mjandernal@piscatawaynj.org; the Township page gives the office address fireprevention@piscatawaynj.org, which is used here. Fire extinguisher: the 2026 MCCC checklist does not list one.

other_items.label: Open or unpermitted work
other_items.detail: Any work done without a required permit must be permitted and all open permits closed before the MCCC is issued, even if a prior owner did the work.

other_items.label: Heating, fireplace, septic and well documents
other_items.detail: If applicable, provide a licensed professional's letter that the heating unit is clean and working, a fireplace letter, septic inspection and clean-out proof, and a passing well water test from a state certified lab.

other_items.label: Finished basement permit
other_items.detail: The MCCC checklist says a finished basement permit is required, even if the basement was finished when the home was bought.

open_questions: Which office issues the state smoke/CO alarm certificate for a Piscataway resale (Fire Prevention Bureau or the MCCC inspection), and its fee and lead time.
How long an MCCC stays valid after it is issued.
